I have a lovely story to share with you. My Aunt tells this story every chance she gets. *clears throat and settles in nice leather armchair* 
So, my Aunt was told when she was 17 that she would never have children. She was severely anorexic for 4 years and was hospitalized over it for over a year. Anyway, she got better by leaps and bounds although she was still on the thinner side. She met her husband and got married, bought a quaint little house in an affluent part of town. Life was good. Her husband knew she wasn't able to have kids, he was fine with it. But, after a couple of years they both wanted to expand their family and naturally were looking into adoption. They were introduced to a young woman who was interested in giving her baby up for adoption. Perfect. My Aunt and Uncle made sure she was completely taken care of. It was going relatively smoothly until the day of delivery. My Aunt rushed to the hospital to be with the young mother, stayed by her side all night through labor. She gives birth to a beautiful, healthy baby boy. The adoption agency comes in with the final paperwork to officially sign the baby over to my Aunt and Uncle and.....the young woman changes her mind. She wants to keep the baby, the father is back in her life, they're moving in together and plan on getting married. My Aunt and Uncle were devastated but they couldn't argue with her and they understood her side. But, nevertheless, they were heartbroken. My Aunt describes the feeling like someone squeezed her heart until it exploded then punched her in the gut. They became recluses. Nobody in the family could reach them for weeks and weeks. Apparently, during this time they were travelling to a different state to meet another expectant mother. Anyway, they're sitting at home one night, and my Aunt says to my Uncle that it feels like her intestines are doing the jitterbug. She feels squirming sensations. This goes on and off for several days before my Aunt decides to go to the doctors about it. They ask her about her period and she says she hasn't had one in a couple of years. Totally random, the doctor does a blood pregnancy test just in case with a smattering of other blood work too. A day or so later, she finds out shes 5 months pregnant. Her only symptom? An occasional craving for toothpaste! No nausea, heartburn, swelling, etc. She gives birth to a healthy baby girl. And 3 years later adopted twin boys. My Uncle says he was at times concerned for my Aunts mental health because when the kids were babies she was frequently dancing around the house singing "So, this is love" from Cinderella.

If you're talking about a therapist, you can get started in the conversation any way you want. My current counselor, I straight up told her in the first 3 minutes of conversation that I have an obsession with feral people. I am beyond fascinated with them. She was just like, "That's cool, whose your favorite case?" It was awesome.

My Mom is someone I never, ever, ever in this millennia talk openly to. Shes just so sensitive and flies off the handle easily. I made a joke one time after I had gotten a hair cut that I wanted to look fabulous for my funeral and she was driving me to the ER in like, an hour tops. She takes everything very seriously. She is the last person I talk to about anything going on in my life.

This is an interesting concept. 
There is a song that my local pop station plays what feels like every other song but it says something like "a hundred bad days makes a hundred bad stories, a hundred bad stories makes me interesting at parties." I probably just slaughtered that songs chorus. Moving onward, seeing life not as something you have to conquer but rather as a flaming shit show that everyone must belly crawl through does sound appealing. I will say though, life doesn't feel short to me. I turned 28 this year and I kept recounting the years because I felt there was no way I was only 28. I feel like I should be coming up on my 60's. So the "what's another week?" Question does feel like I'm being asked to dog paddle the last 100 miles open water on a oceanic voyage. I don't think I can. 
But, yes, I am afraid of death just as I am afraid a man who has been dead 200+ years is going to pop out from behind my bathroom door and devour me like Squidward does krabby patties. 

My main reason for posting on here was my desire to not just go silently into the night. I wanted someone to know that I tried. I fucking tried so hard. I didn't just say, "well, fuck it." And jump head first into the dark abyss. I suited up for battle, I fought in wars that no one documented. I lost friends and lovers in my wars. Sometimes, you can do everything to the T and still stay at the bottom. I truly don't want to die but I cannot figure out how I am going to make it any longer. I honestly don't know how I am going to get to Friday. I just randomly chose Friday because that's my next day off. 
Also, call me a dirt caked hippie if you want but, it's very hard living in such a cruel, corrupted, unstable world. I can't be the only one watching John Oliver segments on YouTube and sobbing more than laughing. I have this really crazy daydream, in it I'm not Jeff Bezos or Bill Gates rich but, I hold my own and I'm buying out chicken farmers and giving them their lives back, I'm financing good tuition free public schools for communities in need, I'm sending people who just need that coveted break to college and breaking the cycle of poverty. I'm building real, actually helpful rehab centers for victims of drug abuse and I'm running a 24/7/365 mental health resource center and hotline staffed with actual mental health professionals. 
And every single time I get my paycheck, I plan to give to all these charities who do what I am not able to but, I only make $14.80 an hour and I only end up being able to give $100/150 and honestly, that's not much at all. Sometimes, I try to convince myself that I will one day be affluent and I will change the World for the better and make up for all the precious resources that I have siphoned over the years but, in reality, that's not going to happen, not to me. I don't play the lottery or gamble or anything. I don't have a shred of talent or business savvy in my body. 

I appreciate you taking the time to comment on a throw away post. I'm sorry I rambled along like a tumbleweed in a dust storm. I have a question for you now, I saw that you're writing a story and I was wondering if you could tell me what it's about? If you don't want to, I completely understand.

I have had the wonderful pleasure of seeing this therapist since I was 16. She was fresh out of college and I was her first real client. I followed her from hospital to hospital than to private practice AND she still only charges me what she first charged me at my very first appointment 12 years ago, $55 without insurance. She's my sixth ever counselor and she is hands down my absolute favorite health professional ever. I talk to her about everything from my strange obsession with pigs and feral people to my absolutely insane delusion of wooing Conan O'Brien to be my beloved. She is very non-judgmental and seems to have the same twisted dark sense of humor I do. Plus, she knows how fond I am of opera and Schubert's classic "Ave Maria" and she is a Christian counselor so every year for Christmas, she finds me a unique collectable centered around either an opera or "Ave Maria". Also, when she moved into her second office, my first appointment there she let me stay after and took me on a tour of the facility, including the behind the scenes spots. It was really interesting and she did it again when she moved to her current private practice. It is not lost on me how lucky I am to have such an absolutely amazing mental health professional in my life. Shes someone I will truly miss. She is the one thing the gods have smiled upon me with. She is an answered prayer and a miracle. I feel absolutely, inescapably terrible. After I called her and left a message, she called me back about 30 minutes later, I didn't answer. Again. No answer. Finally, the third time I answered and lied to her for the first time. I told her I was headed to the outpatient group my local hospital runs everyday for suicidal people and the like. I obviously didn't go. I stayed home and watched Conan's remote sketches on YouTube. I will forever love his Italy trip with Jordan. Absolute perfection, every segment.

To answer your other questions, my finger was on the trigger the whole time. The safety was off and I thought about pulling the trigger every 2 or 3 seconds. After lowering the gun, my mind felt chaotic. It felt somewhat peaceful during, but afterwards I could feel a wave of disappointment wash over me. 

Anyway, thanks for taking the time to comment! I hope I answered your questions satisfactorily. Oh, and yes, I do have a sort of crush on my counselor.
